title: DBH Service Rules — Current Versus Proposed Change and Impact Report
baseline_label: Current effective Ohio Laws rules, live retrieved October 8, 2026
target_label: DBH Service Rules, October 7, 2026 CSI proposal; not operative
overview:
DBH submitted 18 amended service rules to CSI on October 7, 2026; the supplied BIA lists October 14, 2026 as the public comment deadline. The 50-page rule packet remains a proposal marked Draft – Not for Filing. Current authority was retrieved live from Ohio Laws on October 8. No effective date, Medicaid fee schedule, code/modifier transition, or quantified fiscal impact is established by this packet.

The principal operational changes are CPST-to-PSR service redesign under 5122-29-17; adult-focused short-term TBS under 5122-29-18; a three-day weekly minimum for MH day treatment; peer-run organization governance/access/funding requirements; and ACT fidelity waiver/remediation requirements. The day treatment rule remains titled MH day treatment, so a September MH IOP/PHP assumption should not be carried into this DBH scenario without reconciliation.

**Comparison boundary:** This is a complete current-law-to-October-proposal comparison of the 18 supplied rules. The exact September DBH rule text was not recovered; therefore a verified September-to-October rule-by-rule redline is not included. BIA descriptions of stakeholder revisions are reported separately as agency statements, not substituted for that missing baseline.

context_links.label: PDF source manifest and current effective dates

coverage_notes: 18 of 18 supplied rule identifiers matched to live current authority. No rule is classified unchanged solely because the BIA calls all 18 amended; editorial/clarification entries are distinguished below. Six other rules in the fetched 24-rule chapter (5122-29-09, -11, -14, -15.1, -20 and -30) are outside this proposal packet, not inferred rescinded. No separate appendix is included. The September body comparison is unverified.

entries.title: Purpose and applicability
entries.summary: The current purpose provision refers to services certified by the department. The target ties the chapter to the provider definition in 5122-25-01(A). This is an applicability clarification; it does not independently establish Medicaid payment eligibility.
entries.impact: Check which BHBS client agencies and service locations fall under DBH certification.
entries.action: Credentialing: verify applicability against each agency certification.

entries.title: General services
entries.summary: Current (B) and target (C) retain Appendix A credential requirements. Target (C)(1)-(2) adds explicit ASAM third edition level 2.1/2.5 requirements for SUD IOP/PHP. Current (C)(4) and target (D)(4) both require the comprehensive assessment within 30 days; the deadline is retained. Target (D)(1), (D)(6) and (E)(1) expands assessment/treatment language to include gambling and tobacco/nicotine and adds ASAM to standards of care. The 1:12 group counseling ratio remains unchanged: current (D)(3), target (E)(3).
entries.impact: Update assessment and treatment-plan templates without treating the retained 30-day deadline or 1:12 ratio as new requirements. Keep SUD IOP/PHP credential and ASAM checks distinct from MH day treatment.
entries.action: Clinical operations: review assessment templates and SUD IOP/PHP standards; credentialing: obtain the governing Appendix A.
entries.risk: The supplied packet references Appendix A but does not include it. Target (A) calls 5122-25-01 a chapter. Do not infer a revised credential matrix or unrestricted telehealth coverage from this draft.

entries.title: Mental health day treatment service
entries.summary: Current (E) sets 2–7 hours per program day. Target (E) retains 2–7 hours per day and adds at least three days per week. Target (E)(5)-(6) adds treatment/referral capacity for identified medical, psychological or psychiatric needs and ongoing participant monitoring, including level-of-care changes and treatment-plan adjustments. Target (G) specifies an interdisciplinary team and limits each staff member to components appropriate to their credential. The October title and body are MH day treatment, not MH IOP/PHP.
entries.impact: Model at least three program days per week, monitor attendance and staffing capacity, and retain a separate MH day treatment scenario. The daily hours are not new. The draft does not supply a fixed staffing ratio, Medicaid unit calculation, or new rate.
entries.action: Forecast owner: revise the proposed day treatment schedule and monitoring assumptions; clinical operations: map staffing and referral capacity.
entries.risk: Reconcile DBH 5122-29-06 with the October ODM 5160-27-06 proposal before replacing the forecast service model. Neither proposed packet establishes an operative payment policy.

entries.title: Forensic evaluation service
entries.summary: Target (B)(19) adds competency to waive Miranda rights. Current (D)(1) requires the examiner relationship to be explained orally and in writing; target (D)(1) requires an understandable oral explanation, documentation of the process and understanding in the report, and permits a written explanation. Target (E)(5) explicitly records whether the evaluation occurred in person or electronically. Statutory citations and terminology are revised.
entries.impact: Update forensic report templates and consent/confidentiality explanation documentation. These certification requirements do not by themselves make court-related services Medicaid-covered.
entries.action: Forensic program lead: review templates and referral authority.
entries.risk: Target (C)(3) names a regional psychiatric hospital without clearly stating the required order/request; Request clarification of the referral authorization language.

entries.title: Behavioral health hotline service
entries.summary: The 24/7 response, crisis referral, suicide prevention/safety plan, staff training and known-caller documentation duties remain: current and target (A)-(D). Most edits substitute current terminology, including peer support wording, and plain-language obligations rather than introduce a new operating model.
entries.impact: Keep existing hotline coverage and logging controls. Do not book incremental reimbursement based on terminology edits.
entries.action: Crisis operations: confirm existing 24/7 staffing, training and call documentation.

entries.title: Substance use disorder qualified residential treatment program (QRTP) for youth
entries.summary: Target (A)-(C) restates provider/certification scope. Current (B)(3)(f)(i) points to the older JFS resource; target (C)(3)(f)(i) uses the DCY trauma-model resource. Current (B)(7) already requires prehire checks and clearance before presence in the program under 5122-30-31. Target (C)(7) changes the check reference to 5122-26-06(F)(2), while retaining eligibility under 5122-30-31. The 24/7 nursing/clinical availability, six-month aftercare and under-14-day exception are retained rather than newly created.
entries.impact: Review workforce screening, approved trauma model, onboarding and aftercare documentation. Staffing availability and aftercare costs should remain in the baseline where already required.
entries.action: QRTP program/HR leads: validate the screening workflow and trauma-model approval.
entries.risk: The BIA describes additional DCY-guided background checks, but the rule body points to 5122-26-06 and 5122-30-31. Resolve the exact governing checks before implementing a new exclusion list.

entries.title: Crisis intervention service
entries.summary: Current (B) defines a 23-hour observation bed; the target removes that definition and uses (A) for the provider definition. Core crisis evaluation, crisis plan, first aid/CPR, de-escalation and medically unstable referral duties remain in (C)-(E). The target contains no mandatory MRSS/adult crisis referral language.
entries.impact: Preserve core crisis controls. Determine separately how observation and distinct crisis services are certified and paid; absence from this rule is not proof of service elimination.
entries.action: Crisis operations/credentialing: reconcile observation and crisis certification pathways.
entries.risk: Do not infer withdrawal of MRSS or adult crisis rules from omission in this narrower service packet.

entries.title: Driver intervention program
entries.summary: Target (D) expressly lists certification submission materials: operating/program hours and applicable camp/hotel documentation. Target (E) adds peer-service and social-service representatives to the governance/advisory list; annual meetings and minutes are retained. Current (J)(1)(h) requires at least six years of record retention; target (J)(8) increases that minimum to seven years. Much of the long rule reorganizes existing screening, education, meals and ratios; target (Q) retains the 1:15 and 15-person small-group ceiling.
entries.impact: Use a DIP-specific certification and records checklist. Keep program hours and educational ratios distinct from Medicaid counseling rules.
entries.action: DIP program lead: review application materials, governance records, retention and curriculum.
entries.risk: Target (W)-(X) contains overlapping curriculum provisions and source typos. Confirm confidentiality forms against governing federal requirements; this report does not resolve federal legal applicability.

entries.title: SUD case management services
entries.summary: Current (A) requires assessment, referral, monitoring and follow-up as minimum activities; target (A) says activities may include those functions. Target (C) explicitly ties services to a comprehensive individualized treatment plan. Current (B)(1)-(2) says transportation/waiting does not in itself constitute case management; target (D)(1)-(2) lists transportation and waiting as excluded. The long illustrative activity list is removed.
entries.impact: Document the case management intervention and treatment-plan relationship, and separate transportation/waiting time from claimed service time. Do not assume every removed example is forbidden or every restored example is reimbursable.
entries.action: Billing/clinical operations: revise note review and time segregation controls.
entries.risk: BIA question 10 says group settings are allowed, but 5122-29-13 does not expressly state group delivery. Confirm group billing with ODM and the applicable payer; avoid treating the BIA as a payable code/modifier instruction.

entries.title: Peer support services
entries.summary: Target (A)-(D) explicitly addresses members with mental illness/SUD, possible co-occurring intellectual/developmental disability, and caregivers/families; adds recovery, resiliency and wellness definitions; and lists 19 possible activities. Target (H)-(I) retains certified-peer delivery and reporting of disqualifying events. The source retains resiliency/recovery/wellness language described in BIA question 10.
entries.impact: Revise peer templates and staff training around nonclinical, individualized support and family engagement. Preserve certification/reporting controls and verify Medicaid-specific eligibility and documentation separately.
entries.action: Peer program lead/credentialing: crosswalk activities and certification status.
entries.risk: The broader DBH service description does not independently authorize payment for every activity, family encounter or co-occurring condition.

entries.title: Peer run organization service
entries.summary: The current rule sets four broad organizational principles. Target (C)(1) requires recovery supports and certified peer services outside a comprehensive ITP and outside Medicaid/private-insurance third-party reimbursement; grants/contracts/appropriations do not count as reimbursement for this paragraph. Target (C)(3) requires at least 51% lived-experience governing membership, with a caregiver alternative for specified missions. Target (C)(4)-(5) requires predictable published hours and broad community access; (D)-(E) adds mobile-unit and telehealth conditions.
entries.impact: Separate grant-funded peer-run organization activity from reimbursable clinical peer services. Review governance composition, access restrictions, published hours and mobile-unit ownership.
entries.action: Agency leadership/finance: map funding streams; credentialing: verify the certification model.
entries.risk: Do not reduce all agency peer-service revenue to zero. The restriction concerns the peer-run organization service specified in this rule; separately certified Medicaid peer services require their own analysis.

entries.title: Psychosocial rehabilitation service (PSR)
entries.summary: Current 5122-29-17 is CPST. Target (B)-(C) defines PSR and requires agency capacity for all nine listed activity categories, with individualized delivery tied to a comprehensive ITP. It carries forward several CPST-like functions while revising their purpose and evidence requirements. Target (D) permits high-school-diploma staff with relevant training only for (C)(1)(b), (c) and (i). Target (E) permits contracting with another PSR-certified provider; current (D) expressly allows certain delegation to noncertified entities under written agreement.
entries.impact: Map actual CPST/TBS/PSR activities, member needs and rendering-provider qualifications; do not relabel claim codes by rule number. Review subcontractors because the target contracting language is narrower than current CPST delegation.
entries.action: Clinical/billing/credentialing leads: create an activity-by-credential service crosswalk and review subcontractor agreements.
entries.risk: A blanket CPST-to-PSR revenue conversion is unsupported. Agency certification capacity is not the same as each rendering provider eligibility; only three activity categories are explicitly available under the high-school training provision.

entries.title: Therapeutic behavioral services
entries.summary: Current (A)-(B) combines TBS and PSR. Target (B) describes TBS for adults with a mental health diagnosis, intensive one-on-one/group outpatient, short-term and focused on high-risk/disruptive/self-destructive behaviors. Target (C)(1)-(2) details interventions and ongoing monitoring. Target (C)(3) uses degree-qualified practitioners or QBHS under 5122-29-30; current (C)(1)(b) expressly allowed high-school education plus three years relevant experience. PSR moves to target 5122-29-17.
entries.impact: Review youth currently receiving TBS, long-duration services, activity documentation and staff qualifications. Build alternative service scenarios based on member need and approved service eligibility.
entries.action: Clinical/billing leads: identify affected youth and long-duration encounters; credentialing: validate QBHS qualifications.
entries.risk: The draft gives no numeric short-term duration or new fixed group ratio. Do not hard-code an age-transition date, duration cap or rate change absent final adoption and payer instructions.

entries.title: Consultation service
entries.summary: Current (A) defines a formal exchange between a provider and a system outside behavioral health. Target (B) expressly includes community partners such as schools, courts and family members or others who are not established providers of the individual. Target (C)-(D) retains needs surveys, consultation records and qualified staffing.
entries.impact: Clarify consultation documentation and distinguish it from a payable collateral contact under another service definition.
entries.action: Clinical/billing leads: revise the service decision guide and documentation examples.

entries.title: Referral and information service
entries.summary: Target (A) adds the provider definition; remaining (B)-(F) largely retains existing referral follow-up, accessibility/TRS, call logging and separation from hotline crisis assistance. Paragraphs are renumbered.
entries.impact: Maintain referral access, outcome follow-up and logs. No new payable Medicaid benefit is established by these edits.
entries.action: Operations: refresh references in referral policies and preserve current controls.

entries.title: Supplemental behavioral health services
entries.summary: Target (C)(1)-(2) expressly requires service names/descriptions and a support letter from the ADAMH board in each district where services are intended. Current (B)-(C) already contemplates board/department approval and certification, but does not state this application checklist in the same form. Target (D) retains standards, staff orientation and service feedback duties.
entries.impact: Review multi-district agency services and collect district-specific board support before certification applications/updates.
entries.action: Credentialing/agency leadership: inventory supplemental services and board support letters.
entries.risk: Supplemental certification does not create a Medicaid billing code or automatic reimbursement for outreach, screening or representative payeeship.

entries.title: Intensive home based treatment service
entries.summary: Target (C)(1) changes the telehealth reference from 5122-29-31 to 5122-26-22. Target (I) updates the fidelity resource location to ihbtohio.org. The under-21 eligibility, CANS criteria, minimum two FTE, six-month average caseload limits, 24/7 response, practitioner configurations and FFT-only exception remain substantively present.
entries.impact: Update policies/resource links while retaining existing IHBT staffing and caseload assumptions. Confirm operative telehealth authority independently.
entries.action: IHBT lead: update cross-references and verify fidelity review resources.

entries.title: Assertive community treatment services
entries.summary: Target (B) uses severe/persistent mental illness with high service intensity and expressly permits co-occurring diagnoses; current (A) expressly describes major functional impairment/high-risk behavior. Target (E)-(H) retains 3.0 initial and 4.0 within three years fidelity thresholds but specifies preapplication review and waiver or team disbandment for subsequent failure. Waiver submissions require a fidelity action plan and internal steering committee; target (I) ties the plan to quality improvement. Annual review and outreach contact expectations remain. COVID-era discretionary score reductions are removed.
entries.impact: Monitor each ACT team fidelity deadlines and waiver readiness. Include remediation, review and potential team capacity loss in scenarios; do not treat retained scores as newly increased thresholds.
entries.action: ACT program/quality leads: inventory fidelity scores and prepare a waiver remediation workflow.
entries.risk: Current and target certification language does not alone determine Medicaid ACT claim eligibility. Reconcile with ODM 5160-27-04 and payer implementation.

afterword:
### Source status and dates

| Source | Identity/status | Date meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Service-Rules.pdf | Supplied 50-page DBH draft; 18 unique rule headings | PDF created October 7, 2026; not an effective date |
| BIA-Service-Rules.pdf | Supplied 6-page CSI business impact narrative | Submitted October 7; comments end October 14, 2026; no time stated |
| Ohio Laws | Live current HTML for all 18 matched rules and the complete chapter | Retrieved October 8, 2026; individual effective dates are preserved in source copies |
| September DBH proposal | Manifest identifies an earlier 61-page combined packet, but exact source text not recovered | Draft-revision comparison remains unverified |
| Existing ODM ERF report | Repository current/proposed comparison, October 7 | Coordination reference; not DBH authority |

### BIA review and stakeholder revisions

The BIA lists the same 18 identifiers found in the rule packet. Questions 9–10 describe the September 11–18 comment period, stakeholder discussions and October 6 ODM meeting. DBH reports restoring recovery/resiliency/wellness language, restoring SUD case management activity references, removing ambiguous crisis references and “skilled treatment,” adjusting peer-run hours/funding, and clarifying ACT co-occurring eligibility. These statements identify agency-described revisions; without the exact September body they do not establish which individual words changed between drafts.

⚠️ Risk Flag. BIA question 10 mentions prescriber availability when medication management is offered, but the supplied 5122-29-06 contains no express prescriber-availability clause. It also mentions group SUD case management, which 5122-29-13 does not expressly specify. Neither narrative statement should become a hard billing or forecast rule without clarification.

BIA question 1 checks licensing and sanctions but does not check expenditure/reporting or direct revenue/expense impacts. Question 15 nevertheless acknowledges certification fees and employee compliance time without quantifying dollars, hours, affected agency counts or staffing costs. It describes agencies desiring to provide a “new service,” although the package count identifies 18 amended rules and no new rules. Question 10 discusses burden reduction, while question 16 answers “No” to burden-reducing changes. These are gaps for follow-up, not proof of no financial impact. Question 14 promises education after final filing; it supplies no implementation date. No small-business exemption is stated (question 18).

### Forecast and operational actions

| Owner | Action now | Implementation gate |
|---|---|---|
| Forecast owner | Add a DBH October scenario with MH day treatment 2–7 hours/day and at least 3 days/week; keep rates unchanged unless separately sourced. | Final DBH/ODM adoption and rate/payment instructions. |
| Clinical/billing leads | Crosswalk actual CPST/TBS/PSR activities and affected youth; flag credential restrictions and member transition needs. | Final certification and Medicaid code/modifier/provider rules. |
| Credentialing lead | Review PSR capacity, certified subcontractors, TBS QBHS qualifications, QRTP checks and peer-run governance. | Governing appendices, final rules and agency certification changes. |
| Agency leadership/finance | Separate peer-run grant activity from independently billable peer support; estimate compliance labor and ACT remediation costs. | Verified funding agreements and payer coverage. |
| Policy lead | Prioritize comment questions on missing Appendix A, narrative/body mismatches, CPST/PSR transition and age/service continuity. | October 14 deadline listed in supplied BIA. |

DBH regulates certification/service standards; ODM regulates Medicaid coverage/payment. Apply agency certification and rendering-provider qualifications independently. MCO, OhioRISE and MyCare authorization, claims edits and payment details remain payer-specific implementation questions. The packet contains no rates, claim codes, modifiers, units-per-hour conversion, statewide savings estimate or payment go-live. Do not implement live claim edits or replace current law based on this draft.

### Source errors, dependencies and unresolved questions

- Obtain proposed Appendix A to 5122-29-03 before concluding that the rendering-provider matrix changed. The packet has no appendix pages.
- Clarify the erroneous “Chapter 5122-25-01” reference in 5122-29-03(A).
- Clarify 5122-29-07(C)(3) referral authorization referral authorization wording.
- Clarify whether the BIA's medication-management/prescriber and group-case-management statements refer to another rule or omitted text.
- Preserve source typos as evidence. Examples include “substance us disorder” in 5122-29-15(A), “peer run organization ed service” in 5122-29-16(C), and overlapping curriculum requirements in 5122-29-12(W)-(X).
- Determine final transition instructions for agencies, rendering providers, members and subcontractors affected by service remapping. No adoption/effective date is established here.

### Validation and provenance

All 50 rule pages and all 6 BIA pages were extracted. The 18 distinct rule boundaries match the BIA inventory. Blue underlined text and black retained text were included; a drawing-position check found no midline strikeout candidates. Representative pages were visually reviewed. Rule text is reflowed into paragraphs, with source spelling retained and the repeated draft watermark excluded from body text. No numeric-only lines were dropped. All current/proposed bodies are reproduced in the linked full-text companion and hashed by the skill renderer; all relative links and fragments are checked in the delivered package.

Current HTML was fetched through the Ohio Laws extraction skill with a fresh cache. Current-law effective dates range across older rule versions; October 8 is the retrieval date, not a uniform amendment date. Current Appendix A is linked from Ohio Laws but is not reproduced or treated as the missing proposed appendix. No tables/rate schedules were present in the rule-body packet; the BIA header/checkbox form is preserved in its PDF and narrative extract rather than interpreted as a rate table.

The uploaded October PDFs were used directly. A live DBH landing-page retrieval returned 404; therefore the supplied package is not claimed to have been independently byte-matched to the current DBH download. Repository main baseline inspected at commit 5d6c0149d1f9aa5d31f149fda575612ff4d606e9. No AGENTS.md was present in that inspected tree. The report follows the existing ODM report structure. This repository addition preserves current working-law files. The forecast application was not modified.
